chunk_findings.detail: This file is committed to the repository and unconditionally sets `enableAllProjectMcpServers: true`, which auto-approves every MCP server declared in the project's `.mcp.json` without an interactive prompt. `settings.local.json` is by convention a per-user, machine-local override (normally gitignored); committing it forces the setting on every developer and CI checkout that pulls this branch. Concretely: the `enabledMcpjsonServers` allow-list on lines 2-4 is rendered inert, because a later commit that adds a new entry to `.mcp.json` (e.g. a server whose command spawns a shell) is silently trusted and launched on every developer's machine the next time the repo is opened — with no review step and no prompt. The allow-list form (`enabledMcpjsonServers: ["ddflow"]` alone, in `.claude/settings.json`) would have scoped the auto-approval to the one server this change actually needs.
chunk_findings.title: .claude/settings.local.json:5 (`enableAllProjectMcpServers: true`)

chunk_findings.detail: The README gives two mutually exclusive answers about the MCP surface of `search` and `session list|show`. The "Searching everything" section ends with *"No MCP tool yet: it joins the consolidated read tool of the viewers phase; agents use `ddflow_recall` meanwhile"*, and "What is automated" repeats it for sessions: *"No MCP tool yet (planned: `ddflow_list kind=session`)"*. But the "How do I…?" table lists the MCP equivalent of `ddflow search` as `` `ddflow_list` `kind=search` (`query`, `mode`, `sources`, `source`) ``, and the "Listing tasks, phases, bugs and research" section says the opposite of the stale line: *"**Over MCP** these readers, `ddflow session list|show` and `ddflow search` are ONE tool, `ddflow_list` … `kind` is `task | phase | bug | research | session | search`"*. The generated tool table agrees (`ddflow_list` … "`0` = the most: 1000, search 200"). Demonstrating the failure: an agent that reads the search section (as the README instructs agents to read this page) concludes no such tool exists and falls back to `ddflow_recall`, which cannot filter by `--source`/`--kind`/`--state`/`--regex` and therefore cannot run the searches the same page documents with `ddflow search 'lease\.(expired|released)' --regex --kind log`; an agent that reads the "How do I…?" table instead calls a tool the same document says was not built. One of the two statements is stale and it is not possible to tell which from the text.

chunk_findings.detail: The section states two different Python matrices for the same CI job. The job table says *"**tests** | The suite on Python 3.11 and 3.13 — the floor and the current release, because a version-specific break is a break for somebody"*, and the pre-push paragraph agrees (*"It does not run the 3.11/3.13 matrix"*), but the paragraph directly below the table says *"CI's `tests` job runs each matrix Python (3.11, 3.12, 3.13) as a uv-managed standalone build (`uv python install` plus `UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed`)"*. A contributor reproducing CI locally cannot act on this: the instruction "To reproduce locally: `uv python install 3.12` and run `UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed uv run --python 3.12 pytest tests/`" tells them to install a version the table says the job does not run.
chunk_findings.title: README.md — "What CI checks"

chunk_findings.detail: The patch drops the `supers` parameter and deletes the `if f.get("digest") in supers:` branch that appended the `SUPERSEDED: ... do NOT report this finding again; report only a NEW defect of the new code` instruction and `continue`d. `_scope` still populates the `supers` set in the `locals_` dict it is handed (the variable is simply no longer read: `supers, fix = sargs.get("supers")` was removed), so the information that a previous finding's cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed commit is now computed and then discarded. Concrete failure: run a full re-review (`kind == "full"`) of a head where a prior finding's digest is in `supers`. Previously that finding was listed with an explicit "do NOT report this again — report only a NEW defect" instruction; now it is emitted as an ordinary entry with just a `triage:` line, so the model is primed to re-report a defect whose lines no longer exist in the new code, yielding a stale false-positive. This is the behavior the removed block existed to prevent (decision D-gate-economy 3, referenced in the same function's docstring).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_with_previous_findings (deleted `supers` block)

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes the entire regression suite for bug Be1818cd552 — the "supersede findings on rewritten lines / free fix round" behavior (`ddflow.api.review_supersede.changed_old_lines`, `is_superseded`, and the budget accounting around `fix_round`). Nothing in this hunk removes or replaces the guarded behavior: it is a pure deletion of `test_old_side_ranges_and_locations`, `test_a_finding_on_rewritten_lines_is_superseded_not_reraised`, `test_a_finding_on_untouched_lines_is_still_reraised`, `test_a_fix_round_does_not_spend_the_budget` and `test_extensionless_files_and_dash_content_lines`, leaving the fix for Be1818cd552 with no automated check. Any future change to `changed_old_lines` (e.g. an off-by-one in the `@@ -2,4 +2,3 @@` old-line range, or dropping the extensionless-file / `--- old` content-line handling in `p.py`) can silently regress the bug while the suite stays green. Under the recorded rule that ddflow constraints are hard ("must have regression test"), removing the only test that pins this fixed bug's behavior violates that constraint [D-rules-hierarchy]; if instead the whole feature is being intentionally retired, the deletion needs to be accompanied by removal of `ddflow/api/review_supersede.py` in the same change.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_fix_round.py:1 (file deleted)

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement string drops one entry from the recorded `config show` output: the old expectation lists `lease…`, then `review.max_rounds`, `review.settle_all_refuted`, `review.on_exceed`, `review.delta_default`, **`review.fix_round_free`**, `review.combined_under_lines`, `log.reuse_parsed`; the new string jumps straight from `review.delta_default` to `review.combined_under_lines`. Scanning both strings knob by knob, that is the only delta — every other key, value, `source` and `doc` is byte-identical. So this change asserts that `review.fix_round_free` is no longer emitted, while nothing visible in the change demonstrates the knob was removed from the registry, and no surviving entry (e.g. `review.max_rounds`, `review.combined_under_lines`) mentions it either. Given the input this fixture feeds — the replay of that command — the comparison sees a recorded output that no longer contains a knob the CLI still lists, so the test either fails on the missing entry or, if the expectation is regenerated/loosened, quietly stops asserting the knob exists at all; either outcome is wrong for a fixture whose purpose is to pin the exact output. Confirm the knob was actually retired in the same change set (and that no code path still reads `review.fix_round_free`); if it was not, this line must be restored.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (recorded stdout of the `config` step, near `review.delta_default`)

chunk_findings.detail: The recorded transcript for the `--explain` invocation silently drops the whole `review.fix_round_free = True [default]` documentation block (its description, the `ddflow config --set review.fix_round_free false` remedy, and the `DDFLOW_REVIEW_FIX_ROUND_FREE` override). Nothing in this change substantiates the removal: the entry that precedes it (`review.delta_default`) and the one that follows it (`review.combined_under_lines`) are byte-identical between the two sides, so this is not a reordering or a reflow. If the knob still exists in the code (nothing in this hunk removes it), replaying this transcript compares the tool's real output against a fixture that no longer matches, so the test fails; worse, where such transcripts are regenerated rather than asserted, the effect is that `review.fix_round_free` quietly disappears from the documented surface an agent reads, and `DDFLOW_REVIEW_FIX_ROUND_FREE` becomes an undocumented budget knob. Either the code change that deletes `review.fix_round_free` must accompany this fixture update, or this line should be restored.
